actix-http has HTTP/1.1 CL.TE Request Smuggling  — A vulnerability in `actix-http`'s HTTP/1.1 request parser allows an unauthenticated remote client to smuggle requests in deployments where a front-end HTTP intermediary and the Actix backend disagree about whether `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` defines the request body length.

## Severity

**Medium**.
This is an HTTP request smuggling vulnerability that can be triggered over the network without application-level credentials. Exploitation requires a specific proxy topology: an upstream proxy, WAF, load balancer, or similar in

expect.note: actix-http 3.10.0 is Edge's HTTP/1 server parser (actix-web HttpServer, server/src/main.rs:119,205-213). src/h1/decoder.rs:101-150,198-208 accepts a request carrying both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked (TE wins, CL silently ignored, no rejection) -> CL.TE desync with a front proxy that honours CL. Any unauthenticated client reaches the parser; exploitation needs a fronting proxy/LB, common for internet-exposed Edge.

Uncontrolled recursion in the unknown-key skip path of

Then aws-config's credential chain parses JSON from IMDS/ECS/SSO endpoints with aws_smithy_json skip_value for unknown keys (aws-config src/json_credentials.rs:226, sso/cache.rs:293), and skip_inner in aws-smithy-json 0.61.3 src/deserialize/token.rs:305-312 recurses per nesting level without a depth limit. facts.advisory_summary:
bytes has integer overflow in BytesMut::reserve — # Details

In the unique reclaim path of `BytesMut::reserve`, the condition
```rs
if v_capacity >= new_cap + offset
```
uses an unchecked addition. When `new_cap + offset` overflows `usize` in release builds, this condition may incorrectly pass, causing `self.cap` to be set to a value that exceeds the actual allocated capacity. Subsequent APIs such as `spare_capacity_mut()` then trust this corrupted `cap` value and may create out-of-bounds slices, leading to UB.

This behavior is observable in release builds (integer overflow wraps), whereas de

expect.note: Overflow needs BytesMut::reserve(additional) with new_cap+offset > usize::MAX (64-bit). Network-facing reserve calls on the path use bounded sizes: actix-http h1 (h1/mod.rs:61 HW-cap, dispatcher.rs:989, encoder.rs reserves of header/msg lengths), actix-web extractors use with_capacity(8192)/limit-checked buffers (types/json.rs:370, payload.rs:395), h2 hpack reserve is frame-bounded. No attacker-controlled near-usize::MAX reserve found.

facts.advisory_summary: git2 has potential undefined behavior when dereferencing Buf struct  — If the Buf struct is dereferenced immediately after calling new() or default() on the Buf struct, a null pointer is passed to the unsafe function slice::from_raw_parts. According to the safety section documentation of the function, data must be non-null and aligned even for zero-length slices or slices of ZSTs. Thus, passing a null pointer will lead to undefined behavior.

expect.note: git2 only enters via shadow-rs default 'git2' feature; it is used solely by ShadowBuilder in build.rs (build time). Runtime code only reads generated consts (server/src/types.rs:468-482). Buf deref never runs in the deployed binary.

facts.advisory_summary: Potential undefined behavior when calling Remote::list() — When calling `Remote::list()` for a remote of a git repository, when that remote does not advertise any references, git2 passes a null pointer to the unsafe function `slice::from_raw_parts()`. Based on the safety section documentation of function, data must be non-null even for slices of length zero. Thus, the use of a null pointer leads to undefined behavior.

expect.note: git2 via shadow-rs is build-time only (server/build.rs); Remote::list is not called by shadow-rs or Edge at runtime.

facts.advisory_summary: Potential undefined behavior with Signature from a buffer-created BlameHunk — When a `Blame` is created via `Blame::blame_buffer()`, and a `BlameHunk` is retrieved, the pointers to the original author, original committer, final author, and final committer may be null if unavailable. The corresponding `BlameHunk` methods then create `Signature`s based on null pointers; attempting to access the data of the `Signature`s leads to dereferencing null pointers.

expect.note: git2 via shadow-rs is build-time only (server/build.rs); Blame::blame_buffer/BlameHunk not used anywhere.

facts.advisory_summary:
h2 unbounded empty DATA frames — The h2 crate, used internally by hyper, had a flaw that would accept and queue empty DATA frames without limit.
If streams were not actively drained, this could lead to unbounded memory usage, or a panic if the length overflows.

Low severity.

Patched in v0.4.16.

expect.note: h2 0.3.26 is actix-http's HTTP/2 server (actix-web default 'http2' feature). HTTP/2 is offered only on the TLS listener via ALPN (main.rs:202-206 bind_rustls_0_23 when --tls-enable/TLS_ENABLE; plain bind uses .tcp() = HTTP/1 only). With Edge TLS enabled, any client can send empty DATA frames; recv.rs:660-666 pushes every DATA frame (incl. zero-length) to pending_recv without limit, and many handlers (GET endpoints) never drain the body. Not reachable in default plain-HTTP config; reachable in the common TLS-on-Edge config.

  - 8192 bytes total

`ref_prefix` or `init_using_dict`) or a dictionary table (`ref_ddict` with
`RefMultipleDDicts`) ended up with both copies freeing it. A context cloned
mid-frame resumed on uninitialized stream state. The clone also silently lost
the `WindowLogMax` limit.

The flaw was corrected by refusing to clone such contexts, and by carrying
over the parameters the copy leaves out.

expect.note: DCtx::try_clone is behind 'experimental', not enabled.

facts.advisory_summary:
Out-of-bounds read with an out-of-range `InBuffer::pos` — `InBuffer`'s fields are public, so safe code can set `pos` past the end of
`src`. The position was passed to the C library unchecked, and
`ZSTD_seekable_compressStream`, unlike the other streaming functions, does
not validate it: it read past the end of the input slice, by up to the
frame size, and compressed that memory into the output.

The flaw was corrected by checking the position before every call into the
C library.

expect.note: SeekableCStream requires 'seekable' feature, not enabled.
